blindSummary: Same-sex conduct is legal and no law targets trans presence, but this state/province is one of six states/provinces whose legislature has refused to create any legal gender recognition procedure (a major human-rights organisation, March 2025). The practical consequence is permanently mismatched identity documents for trans people - a core visitor-relevant legal fact, since document mismatch is what triggers questioning at checkpoints - with no local procedure to cure it; courts can order recognition case by case. The neighbouring state/province (where a major human-rights organisation documented mistreatment of trans people in state institutions) indicates a conservative institutional climate. There is no dedicated violence signal of its own.
blindSourceSummaries: A major human-rights organisation's state-by-state tracker on legal gender recognition (March 2025), covering which of the country's 32 states/provinces have legislated an administrative procedure and the highest court rulings that drove expansion. Lists this unit among the ten of 32 states/provinces that had NOT reformed legislation to create a legal gender recognition procedure as of March 2025.

A major human-rights organisation's report (6 March 2024) on a neighbouring state/province: the absence of a legal gender recognition procedure there exposes trans people to institutional maltreatment - the August 2023 killing of a trans activist remained unsolved, hate-motivation provisions are absent from that state/province's criminal code, and healthcare staff routinely out patients by calling legal names. A baseline for how a non-reforming state/province behaves.

A major newspaper report (24 July 2024) on the national capital district making transfemicide a crime with sentences up to 70 years (approved 18 July 2024), in one of the deadliest settings for trans people in the region; over 95% of homicides nationally went unpunished in 2022.
blindOutOfScope: General cartel violence, kidnapping and theft drive foreign travel advisories for parts of the country and affect all travellers equally; they do not move trans-specific risk here.
blindLocalsOnly: The absence of a legal gender recognition procedure bites hardest on residents' documents and registry dealings; visitors use home documents and never apply locally.
